note: Everyday Israel games (src/games/g4-*). Every Hebrew line here is copied from the app's own data: src names the file and record (phrasebook, lessons, dialogues, words, vocab5000, the calendar days file, the register ladder or the scenarios file). slice keeps only some words of the source; strip takes a prefix and suffix off; parts joins two copied entries. Nothing was retyped. The sources are drafts that still need a native speaker's review; review notes are carried over. Tests (tests/games.g4.test.js) re-check every copy.
composed: Clock Talk shows each hour as t.thehour then a counting number nf1 to nf10 side by side (for 3 and 7 this equals the phrasebook and lesson I-19 lines exactly; the others need review).
Read It Back reads phone digits with the counting numbers nf1 to nf9 and nf0 (zero, from vocab5000): owner to confirm this is how numbers are read out.
Falafel Stand shows f.without next to a topping (bli plus the food word) as two chips.
Pill Box shows ph.against next to a complaint, and ph.before or ph.after next to f.meal, as separate words on the label.
Ring the Bell shows b.next, a colon, then the stop name.
Open or Closed? and Week Planner show Friday as day.fri (erev Shabbat).
